title: On‑prem manifest sanitizer, safe rollback and operator preflight for stuck tenant upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers on Private/VPC upgrades reported stuck Helm upgrades and operator reconciliation failures. Root causes appear to be manifest timestamp skew and non-idempotent hook reapplication leading to config drift and orphaned KV entries. This ticket implements a runtime manifest sanitizer + operator preflight checks, a safe rollback annotation for tenants, and a targeted hotfix image to unblock in‑flight upgrades without mass tenant rollbacks.
steps_to_reproduce: Install operator v1.54 with preexisting tenant CRs using Helm v3.8
Trigger an in‑place tenant upgrade via the customer upgrade API (simulated with upgrade annotation on Tenant CR)
Run a concurrent onprem operator image rotation (simulate network pause / kube-apiserver latency)
Observe: Helm release stuck in PendingInstall or PostUpgrade hook failing; operator CrashLoopBackOff or long reconcile loops; tenant namespace contains duplicated hook jobs and stale kv-schema keys
Inspect: manifest timestamps differ between Helm release object and actual resources; finalizers left orphaned on hook jobs
proposed_solution: Implement a conservative manifest sanitizer in the onprem operator that normalizes resourceCreate/timestamp fields used during Helm diff comparisons and skips non‑deterministic annotation checks. Add a preflight step that detects locked helm.lock objects and exposes a diagnostics endpoint. Add a Tenant CR annotation @redwood.io/safe-rollback=true which triggers a coordinated, idempotent rollback path: cancel stuck hooks, requeue reconcile with sanitized manifests, and run a small migration to reconcile KV schema versions. Ship a hotfix operator image operator-2026.03.1 with these changes and a migration job binary (kvmigrate) that can be run in customer clusters.
rollback_plan: If hotfix causes regressions, operator fleet has an automated staged rollback: 1) Pause automatic upgrades via console feature flag 'private.upgrades.autopilot=false', 2) Roll operator image back to last known good tag (operator-2026.02.5) in 5% canary -> 25% -> 100% progression, 3) For impacted tenants still stuck, mark Tenant CR with annotation @redwood.io/manual-recover=true and run manual recovery playbook documented in runbook link, 4) Notify customers and schedule customer‑facing remediation windows.
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest sanitizer normalizing fields; integration tests that simulate Helm hook replay and verify idempotence; e2e on-prem cluster runbook exercise with a synthetic tenant upgrade and network latency injection; canary rollout to internal staging Private clusters (3 tenants) followed by a 10% customer canary cohort for 48 hours. Metrics to monitor: operator reconcile latency, number of stuck Helm releases, number of orphaned finalizers, tail latency on upgrade APIs.
acceptance_criteria: A sanitizer module merges into operator with <5% added reconcile CPU under load
Automated test reproducer demonstrates stuck upgrade resolved in >= 95% of runs
Hotfix image built, signed, and available in private registry; helm chart bumped to operator-2026.03.1
Runbook updated with step‑by‑step remediation and Slack escalation playbook
Canary rollout completes with no new data‑loss customer reports; telemetry shows reduction in stuck upgrades

notes: Prefer conservative normalization: only rewrite fields that Helm uses for equality checks (managedFields timestamps, lastAppliedConfig) to avoid masking customer changes.
Avoid aggressive deletion of hook jobs; prefer backoff and bounded retry with idempotent cleanup steps to prevent data loss.
Plan to add telemetry events: sanitized_manifest_applied and sanitization_reverted for auditability.
Customer communication templates drafted in PM review; ensure legal signoff before any forced migrations on customer clusters.
